plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.3.4
plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the shell method for computing volumes of solids of revolution about the y-axis. Panel (a): the 2D xy-plane showing a decreasing curve with a single rectangular strip Rk spanning from x_{k-1} to xk approximating the kth vertical strip of the region; a rotation arrow near the y-axis indicates revolution about that axis. Caption: Rectangle approximating the kth strip. Panel (b): a 3D view of the cylindrical shell Sk generated by revolving the rectangle about the y-axis, shown as a hollow cylindrical ring. Caption: Cylindrical shell generated by the rectangle. The figure introduces the shell method by showing how each thin vertical rectangle, when revolved, produces a cylindrical shell whose volume approximates the corresponding tubular portion of the solid.

demo_steps.title: Start with the kth rectangle
demo_steps.narration: Panel (a) shows one vertical strip R_k under the decreasing curve. Its width is Delta x and its height is the function value used for the shell.

demo_steps.title: Revolve the same strip
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the shell view. The rectangle has swept around the y-axis to form S_k, with radius r_k, height h_k, and thickness Delta x.

demo_steps.title: Compare rectangle and shell
demo_steps.narration: The linked comparison highlights the same k in both views, showing that moving the strip farther from the y-axis increases the shell circumference.

demo_steps.title: Refine the approximation
demo_steps.narration: Increasing n makes the shells thinner. The displayed shell-sum volume moves closer to the exact shell-method integral.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use Three.js coordinates with +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, and +Z depth. Model the 2D region in the XY plane at z=0, revolved about the y-axis. World-space axes: x from 0 to 5.2 units and y from 0 to 4.2 units. Use interval a=0.8 to b=4.4. Function curve: f(x)=3.25 - 0.13*x^2 over [0.8,4.4], clipped above y=0; it should appear as a smooth teal decreasing, concave-down curve similar to the source. For n strips, Delta x=(b-a)/n. Strip k has x_{k-1}=a+(k-1)Delta x, x_k=a+k Delta x, radius r_k=(x_{k-1}+x_k)/2, height h_k=f(x_k), and shell volume Delta V_k=2*pi*r_k*h_k*Delta x, equivalent to pi*(x_k^2-x_{k-1}^2)*h_k. Clamp stripIndex to n if the user lowers n below k. True volume for the chosen curve is V=2*pi*integral_a^b x(3.25-0.13x^2) dx = 2*pi*[1.625x^2 - 0.0325x^4]_a^b. Panel (a): rectangle R_k is vertical, pale teal fill #b7dfd8 with opacity about 0.75, gray outline #666666, label in dark gray/black. Curve color #22bfc0 with thick stroke. Rotation arrow near the upper left y-axis is black/dark gray. Panel (b): cylinder axis is the y-axis; selected shell is annular cylinder between radii x_{k-1} and x_k, height h_k, centered on y-axis, with bottom at y=0 and top at y=h_k. Shell material pale teal #9fd8d3 with opacity 0.45. Reference neighboring shells or full solid approximation should be translucent light gray #d9dcdf with opacity 0.25, with gray outline ellipses #777777. The source view shows the cylinder front-on with visible top and bottom ellipses; use an orthographic/axonometric camera looking from positive z with slight elevation so ellipses are visible and the y-axis remains vertical. In linked comparison, place panel (a) on the left and panel (b) on the right, matching the source composition, with generous spacing and caption boxes beneath each panel.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement shell geometry as two open cylinders plus annular top and bottom surfaces, or as a custom BufferGeometry with radial segments. Use transparent rendering with depthWrite disabled for translucent shell surfaces so inner and outer outlines remain visible. Draw ellipse outlines using LineLoop curves at y=0 and y=h_k for both inner and outer radii. Keep labels as screen-facing sprites or CSS2D labels. On stripCount changes, rebuild or rescale the partition rectangles/shells and recompute the shell-sum volume. In panel (b), allow drag rotation only for the 3D shell group/camera; panel (a) remains fixed. In linked comparison, the stripIndex slider should update both the 2D rectangle highlight and the 3D shell highlight simultaneously.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for strip index k: select the kth rectangle in panel (a) and simultaneously highlight the corresponding cylindrical shell Sₖ in panel (b), displaying its radius, height, and volume
- Slider for number of strips n: increase n and watch the shells become thinner, with the total shell volume sum converging to the true solid volume

authoredInteractions:
- Slider for strip index k: select the kth rectangle in panel (a) and simultaneously highlight the corresponding cylindrical shell Sₖ in panel (b), displaying its radius, height, and volume

authoredContext: As a rule, the tubes will have curved upper surfaces, so there will be no simple formulas for their volumes. However, if the strips are thin, then we can approximate each strip by a rectangle (Figure 5.3.4a). These rectangles, when revolved about the y-axis, will produce cylindrical shells whose volumes closely approximate the volumes of the tubes generated by the original strips (Figure 5.3.4b). We will show that by adding the volumes of the cylindrical shells we can obtain a Riemann sum that approximates the volume V, and by taking the limit of the Riemann sums we can obtain an integral for the exact volume V .

discrepancies: The default rendered view shows only panel (a), whereas the source figure presents panels (a) and (b) side by side; the linked comparison option exists but is not the initial composition.
Panel (a) adds many faint neighboring rectangles/strips under the curve, while the source shows only the single highlighted rectangle R_k.
The selected rectangle R_k is much narrower than in the source, causing x_{k−1} and x_k to appear crowded and reducing resemblance to the textbook strip.
Panel (b) in the code includes multiple nested reference cylinders and a numeric callout/readout, whereas the source shows a simpler transparent cylindrical shell with only the S_k label.
The generated figure adds pedagogical UI/readouts for convergence, shell volume, radius, height, and strip count that are not part of the original visual design.
evaluation.notes: The core shell-method geometry is correct and interactive, but the default composition and added approximation machinery make it less faithful to the simple two-panel textbook figure.
action_items: Make the default view the side-by-side linked comparison so panels (a) and (b) match the source composition immediately.
Remove or greatly fade the extra partition rectangles in panel (a), leaving the single highlighted R_k rectangle as in the source.
Use a wider selected rectangle by default so x_{k−1} and x_k are separated similarly to the source.
Simplify panel (b) by removing the numeric callout and excess nested cylinders, keeping one transparent cylindrical shell and the S_k label.
plan_action_items: Revise the plan to prioritize faithful reproduction of the static two-panel textbook composition over added convergence-analysis controls and readouts.

feedback.rationale: The core concept is correct, and the problems are mainly implementation-level faithfulness issues—default layout, extra rectangles/cylinders/readouts, and rectangle scale—that the generator can fix without a new conceptual plan.
